the generation of 5-micron electron beam with energy 1 MeV and current 1 A is feasible.
the generation of the electron probe with energy up to 100 keV and current up to 100 mA has been demonstrated.

the electron beam generation and characterization system described in this paper has demonstrated the possibility to produce a 5 micron electron beam at 1.2 MeV energy.
the electron beam with parameters: current density 1.5 A/cm2, energy 100 keV, pulse duration 100 ps, pulse repetition rate 100 Hz was obtained.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the method for generation of electron beams with energy up to 1 MeV, current up to 10 kA, duration up to 10 ns, and transverse size up to 5 microns.
we have successfully demonstrated a new type of electron beam generation and acceleration scheme, which is based on the interaction between a high power laser and a plasma waveguide.
we have generated the 5 micron electron beam probe with 10 psec pulse duration and 1.5 pC pulse energy, and we have demonstrated the electron beam probe to measure the optical scale structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron beam probe has the parameters which are comparable with parameters of laser pulses.
the beam can be generated and transported in a way that allows it to probe optical structures.

the electron beam with the parameters of 5 micron in size and 0.1-1 pico-Coulombs of charge per pulse could be generated by using the compact accelerator with the parameters of the electron beam of 5 MeV, 1 nC, 100 psec, 100 kV/cm.
